breaking_changes.BC_description: The `Command.parse()` method now treats excess command-line arguments as errors by default. Previously, excess arguments (arguments not declared in the command definition) were silently allowed. The default value of the 'allowExcessArguments' setting has changed from true to false in Commander v13.0.0.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: To handle this breaking change, either: 1) Declare all expected arguments in your command definition using `program.argument('[args...]', 'description')`, or 2) Explicitly allow excess arguments by calling `program.allowExcessArguments()` before parsing.

breaking_changes.BC_description: Commander now throws an error during Option construction for unsupported option flags, including: 1) multiple characters after a single dash (e.g., '-abc'), and 2) multiple long flags in a single Option. Prior to this change, these invalid formats were silently accepted but may not have worked as expected.

Multiple calls to `.parse()` will now throw an error if `storeOptionsAsProperties: true` is set. When using default settings (`storeOptionsAsProperties: false`), multiple calls to `.parse()` are now supported through automatic state management.
The `Help.wrap()` method has been removed and refactored into `formatItem()` and `boxWrap()` methods for better support of text styling and ANSI color sequences.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace calls to `Help.wrap()` with the new `boxWrap()` method for general text wrapping that properly handles ANSI escape sequences. For example, change `helper.wrap(commandDescription, helpWidth, 0)` to `helper.boxWrap(commandDescription, helpWidth)`. The `boxWrap()` method handles text wrapping with proper support for ANSI color sequences and no longer requires the third parameter (indent) that was present in the old `wrap()` method.
